title: Infosys CEO says AI could account for half of company’s work within three years
key_facts: Salil Parekh, Infosys chief executive and managing director, spoke at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum 2026 on Tuesday 13 October.
AI services were more than 8% of revenue last quarter and grew at a double-digit rate sequentially.
He said the share could be 20 to 30% of work in a few quarters, and almost half in two or three years.
Infosys hired 20,000 graduates last year and plans another 20,000 this financial year.
About 80,000 of its roughly 300,000 staff already work with coding tools on client projects.
He warned of cheaper models, costly chips, data sovereignty limits and a possible public backlash against AI infrastructure.
quote_evidence: "It (AI services) is growing at a fantastic pace."
"Today the demand is fantastic, but these are some of the risks that could play out," Parekh said.
why_it_matters_hint: An Indian IT services chief expects AI work to become a large share of his firm's business.
notes: Remarks dated 13 Oct 2026 (before the window). Eastern Eye does not name the wire it drew on.
